Kremlin officials are today praising a decision

and has this report.
Just blocks from the Capitol building,
about two dozen people huddle around
an official ballot drop box.

who gathered for the national No King's Vote Early Day of Action.

Cheers rang out as each person slid their ballot into the box.
The group hopes people across the country

Ava Berger and PR News, Washington.
Doctors have discharged Pope Leo from hospital in Rome
after just five days.
As the villain Marx reports, medical staff say
the operation to remove a part of his lung
that tested positive for cancer was successful.
Pope Leo left the Jamelli hospital in central Rome
waving to well-wishers outside as he walked out unaided,
flanked by officials and security guards in dark suits.
The Vatican press office released a statement
outlining details of the surgery from his own personal physician
as well as the hospital's chief of thoracic surgery,
who led the team that operated on the pontiff.
Those two doctors say the Pope had undergone blood tests
and a chest x-ray Saturday morning,
with the results confirming his clinical condition
meant he could leave hospital.
The Vatican says Leo's post-operative recovery time
had been faster than scheduled.
He's expected to lead the Angelus prayer

For NPR News, I'm Villa Marx.
And you're listening to NPR from New York City.
White House Press Secretary Katie Zachariah

President Trump said he talked to her on Friday,
telling her she didn't have to do the job

White House reporters asked Zachariah about her law degree,

Authorities in England held an emergency summit this week
to discuss a climate-related phenomenon,
a huge number of octopus multiplying in British waters.
And Paris-Laurent Frere reports from London.
Fissures and scientists are trying to cope
with what they call an octopus bloom,
a nearly 1,500 percent increase in octopus
caught off the coast of southwest England
over the past five years.
Warming sea temperatures mean that animals
are migrating farther north from Europe.
For some in England's fishing industry, it's a boon.
They're exporting record numbers to France and Spain,
where octopus is more common on menus.
But shellfish here have been decimated
because octopus eat crabs, lobsters, clams and mussels.
Businesses that farmer catch those creatures have been hit hard.
Animal welfare groups, meanwhile,
caution against the exploitation

Lauren Freire, NPR News, London.
